name: toolsmith-pr-land
intent: Merge a pull request, then return the local clone to its updated base branch.
use_when: A pull request is approved and green, and the next step is to merge it and carry on from the updated base branch.
You would otherwise chain `gh pr merge`, `git checkout main`, `git pull` and `git branch -D`.
not_for: Waiting for CI first: run toolsmith-ci-wait --pr N before this.
Merging when tracked files have uncommitted changes: commit or stash them first.
input: No stdin. N is the pull request number; without it, the pull request of the current branch. Runs in the repository's directory, with `gh` installed and signed in, and the GitHub remote named origin.

options.text: Rebase the commits onto the base. Without one of these three, the repository's only allowed method is used; when it allows several, the tool asks you to choose.

output: 'Merged #N "title" into <base> (<method>).', then the clean-up: the head branch is deleted on origin and locally, the base branch is checked out and fast-forwarded to origin, and its new tip is shown. When open pull requests or local branches were built on the head branch, it lists the commands to move them: `git rebase --onto <base> <old head commit> <branch>` and `gh pr edit <n> --base <base>`. It does not run those.

exit_codes.text: Merged, and the local clone is on the updated base branch.
Nothing merged: uncommitted changes, the pull request is not open or is a draft, or gh could not merge it.
The arguments are wrong, or the repository allows several merge methods and none was chosen.
Merged, but a clean-up step failed; the message names the git command that failed.

examples.title: Merge the current branch's pull request and clean up
examples.situation: On branch empty-results, whose pull request #7 targets main. The repository allows only squash merges, and pull request #8 (results-filters) was built on empty-results.
examples.setup:
set -e
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=Dev GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=dev@example.com GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Dev GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=dev@example.com
git init -q . && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main
o=.git/test-origin
git init -q "$o" && git -C "$o" symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main
echo '# Shop' > "$o/README.md" && git -C "$o" add README.md && git -C "$o" commit -qm Start
git -C "$o" checkout -qb empty-results && echo 'No results yet.' > "$o/results.txt" && git -C "$o" add results.txt && git -C "$o" commit -qm 'Show empty results' && git -C "$o" checkout -q main
git remote add origin "$PWD/$o" && git fetch -q origin
git checkout -q -b empty-results origin/empty-results && git branch -q --track main origin/main
examples.stdout_regex:
\AMerged #7 "Show empty results" into main \(squash\)\.
Deleted branch empty-results on origin and locally\.
main is now at [0-9a-f]{7} Show empty results \(#7\)
Branches built on empty-results need a rebase onto main:
  git rebase --onto main [0-9a-f]{40} results-filters
  gh pr edit 8 --base main
\z
examples.stdout_sample:
Merged #7 "Show empty results" into main (squash).
Deleted branch empty-results on origin and locally.
main is now at 4f2c1d9 Show empty results (#7)
Branches built on empty-results need a rebase onto main:
  git rebase --onto main 9b1e0c4d2a7f3e8b6c5d4a3f2e1d0c9b8a7f6e5d results-filters
  gh pr edit 8 --base main

examples.title: Uncommitted changes stop it before the merge
examples.situation: The same branch, with an edit to README.md that is not committed.
examples.setup:
set -e
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=Dev GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=dev@example.com GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Dev GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=dev@example.com
git init -q .
echo '# Shop' > README.md && git add README.md && git commit -qm Start
echo 'draft' >> README.md
examples.stderr: toolsmith-pr-land: tracked files have uncommitted changes; commit or stash them first. Nothing was merged.
